content: Azelaic acid gel is prescribed to reduce the bumps, lesions, and swelling associated with rosacea, a skin condition characterized by redness, flushing, and pimples on the face. Azelaic acid cream is used to treat acne. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as dicarboxylic acids. It treats acne by eliminating bacteria that infect pores and by reducing the production of keratin, a natural substance that can contribute to acne formation. However, the exact mechanism by which azelaic acid treats rosacea is not fully understood. Azelaic acid is available as a gel or cream for topical application. It is typically applied twice daily, once in the morning and once in the evening. To ensure consistent use, apply it at the same times each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use azelaic acid exactly as directed. Do not apply more or less of it, or use it more frequently than prescribed. While azelaic acid helps control acne and rosacea, it does not cure these conditions. It may take four weeks or longer to experience the full benefits of the medication. Continue using it as directed, even if you do not notice significant improvement initially. To apply the cream or gel, follow these steps: 1. Wash the affected skin with water and a mild soap or a soap-free cleansing lotion, then pat it dry with a soft towel. Consult your doctor for a recommended cleanser, and avoid using alcoholic cleansers, tinctures, abrasives, astringents, or peeling agents, especially if you have rosacea. 2. Apply a thin layer of the cream or gel to the affected skin. Gently and thoroughly massage it into the skin. Take care to avoid contact with your eyes or mouth. If the medication gets into your eyes, rinse them with plenty of water and contact your doctor if irritation occurs. 3. Do not cover the treated area with bandages, dressings, or wrappings. You may apply non-irritating makeup over the medication once it has dried. 4. Wash your hands with soap and water after handling the medication. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using azelaic acid, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to azelaic acid or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had any medical conditions. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using azelaic acid, contact your doctor. Be aware that azelaic acid may cause changes in skin color, particularly in individuals with darker complexions. Notify your doctor if you notice any changes in your skin color. If you have rosacea, avoid foods and beverages that trigger flushing or blushing, such as alcoholic drinks, spicy foods, and hot drinks like coffee and tea. If you have acne, maintain your normal diet unless otherwise instructed by your doctor. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Azelaic acid may cause side effects. Common side effects include itching, burning, stinging, and tingling at the application site. Inform your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Rarely, azelaic acid may cause a rash. If you experience this or any other unusual problems, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store azelaic acid in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
